verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The second half is the Lean formula verbatim: HeatedOutgoing.Pi is -(1/2)∫_{(X,∞)} E(x,η)^2/x dx, which is -∫_X^∞ E(x,η)^2/(2x) dx, same sign, same constant, same lower limit, same integrand, normalised at radial infinity. The first half is stated in inner coordinates rather than in r: radialPartial_pressure gives ∂_X Π = f^2, and with E = √(2X) f (ProfileHistories.Profiles.E) this is ∂_X Π = E^2/(2X); the rewriting to the paper's line is the chain rule in X = r^2/(2q) together with the paper's own p^{(0)} = q^{-2A}Π and u_θ^{(0)} = q^{-A}E, which give ∂_r p^{(0)} = q^{-2A}(r/q)∂_XΠ and (u_θ^{(0)})^2/r = q^{-2A}(r/q)f^2 — the same identity. One encoding difference, recovered rather than lost: Profiles.pressure is built as pressure0(η) + ∫_0^X f^2, an antiderivative normalised at the axis with a free smooth function pressure0, not at X = ∞; actual_base_compatible pins pressure0 to outgoing.axisDatum = -(1/2)∫_0^∞ E^2/x dx = Π(0,η), so the two normalisations agree. pressureCoefficient_eq_zero_iff is the same balance inside the slow expansion (at n = 0 the convolution is φ_0^2 and the `previous` term is empty).
